name: TeamClu
tagline: Shared skills and group chat for your team's AI agents.
_descriptionLimit: PH's composer caps Description at 500 characters (the kit's 779-char 'mid' text does NOT fit). This is the team-story version, 415 chars.
description:
TeamClu is a shared workspace where your team and its AI agents work in the same group chats.

Sessions are group chats, not 1:1 bot chats: add teammates, @mention people, branch an agent reply into a thread, and see who's online.

Skills are team assets: publish one with a changelog and every teammate's agent follows it automatically. Edit locally and you get a conflict, never a silent overwrite.

MIT, in beta.
story:
I kept running into the same thing on every team I worked with: the AI agent is personal, and that's the wrong shape for a team.

I'd teach my agent how we run a release. A teammate would teach theirs the same thing a month later, slightly differently. And the work itself happened in a chat window nobody else could see.

So TeamClu makes two things shared instead of private.

Skills are team assets. You publish one to your team's registry with structured metadata and a changelog, and every teammate's agent follows it automatically — when you fix a broken step, the fix actually reaches people instead of dying in your dotfiles.

Sessions are group chats. Not 1:1 chats with a bot: add teammates, @mention people, see who's online, and branch any agent reply into its own thread. The agent is a participant, not a service.

Knowledge, roles and MCP config are shared the same way, and each member still keeps a private context. Agents run on your own machines, reachable from WeCom, Feishu, Discord, KOOK, WeChat or Email.

It's MIT licensed and in beta — built in the open, and I'd rather hear where it breaks than where it's nice.
